_**User**_

The ElPicker Panel that appears upon pick needs a better, more compact layout. Right now it is often too tall to usefully fit on the screen. I we do not want both a Show Code and an upper element area. The new, all-in-one Element area should now show a concise tree of haml-style selectors that is inherently scrolled to the bottom (the selected item) and detects the presence of our special semantic classes. Rows with non-semantic classes just list those verbatum and are quite tiny. The ability to scroll horizontally or tooltip these can help us explore. Clicking any row copies just the selector.
If an element has a semantic tag, the semantic tag goes first and is bigger font followed by dim text with all the classes. Clicking the semantic tag just copies it. Clicking the dim part copies all the classes.
We can have tabs above our Element scrollable area for the other ways of expressing the selector, but they should be height: 12px; and and unobtrusively small text font. The first tab is called "Smart" and uses the logic we describe above. 
Each Smart Element row for the tree has:
- Element tag (i.e. div, img,) is red and first (tiny)
- Semantic tag, bigger, click-to copy just this class string, may be absent for an element with no semantic classes. 
- Tiny rest of the classes spills wide. Tooltip of tag + classes with useful wrapping. Click to copy all classes of the element.
- Toasts what you copied.

Tooltip, copy toast, and tiny "rest of classes" use a clever way to render the string where we get a simple hue shifting sequence so each class has a next color. Use simple prime hue roation function to map index of the split parts into a rainbow of unlikely to repeat colors through syncapation of shift.

All changes are complete. Here's a summary of what was done:

### Panel Layout Overhaul

**Removed** (for compactness):
- Breadcrumb bar
- Navigation hint text
- Separate "Element" preview section
- "Show Code" toggle + code section
- Suggested Classes chip panel
- Format dropdown in action bar

**Added** (the new compact all-in-one design):

1. **Tiny tabs** (12px height, 7px font) above the scrollable area: `Smart | S.CSS | S.XPath | CSS | XPath | Outer | Inner`. Tabs switch between the Smart tree view and raw selector/HTML text views.

2. **Smart tree view** showing the ancestor chain from `<body>` down to the selected element, auto-scrolled to the bottom. Each row:
   - **Tag** (`div`, `span`, etc.) in red, 8px
   - **Semantic classes** (`xx--*`, `oo--*`) in green, 10px bold — click copies just that class
   - **Rest of classes** in 7px hue-shifted rainbow colors — click copies all classes (space-separated)
   - **Row click** (on tag/whitespace) copies the full haml-style selector: `tag#id.class1.class2`

3. **Prime hue rotation** via `(i * 137 + 30) % 360` — uses the golden angle approximation for maximally distinct sequential colors. Applied to:
   - The tiny "rest of classes" spans in each tree row
   - The tooltip (hover over rest-of-classes shows tag + all classes with wrapping and color)
   - The copy toast (dark-bg toast shows colored class spans)

4. **Tooltip** with hue-colored classes appears on hover over the dim class area, showing the full tag + semantic + rest in a wrapped layout.

5. **Two toast styles**: green for simple messages, dark-bg with colored spans for class-copy actions.

6. **Header/actions made more compact** — smaller padding, smaller icons, "Reselect" shortened to "Re".
